title: Rectangle Area via Constructor
prompt_md:
## Goal
Define a `Rectangle` class whose constructor takes a width and a height and stores them, plus an `area()` member function. Using a constructor means a `Rectangle` is always fully initialized the instant it is created — there is no window where it exists but its dimensions are unset.

## Input
Two positive integers on one line: width and height.

## Output
One line: `Area: <value>`, the width times the height.

## Feature
This exercises constructors: a constructor with parameters that initializes the object's data members at creation time.

title: Label with Overloaded Constructors
prompt_md:
## Goal
Define a `Label` class that can be created two ways: with no arguments (giving it the default text `untitled`) or with a string argument (giving it that text). This is constructor overloading — two constructors that differ in their parameter lists.

## Input
First line: an integer mode. If it is `0`, the program constructs a default `Label`. Otherwise, a second line contains a single word used to construct the `Label`.

## Output
One line: the label's text.

## Feature
This exercises overloaded constructors: a default (no-argument) constructor and a one-argument constructor coexisting in the same class, selected by how the object is created.
